intro: まで draws a finishing line: the point in space or time where something stops. On its own it covers the whole stretch up to that line (work until five, walk as far as the station). Add に and the line becomes a deadline: までに says something happens at some moment before the line, not all the way to it.

skills.rule: The point where a stretch of distance or time ends takes まで: until, as far as, up to.
skills.explain:
まで marks where something stops. In time, the action or state continues right up to that point: 五時まで働く (work until five), 来週まで日本にいる (be in Japan until next week). In space, the movement covers the distance up to that place: 駅まで歩く (walk as far as the station). It pairs naturally with から for the start: 九時から五時まで. The end point is included: 金曜日まで休み means Friday is a day off too.

まで attaches to any time word, including relative ones that refuse に: 明日まで, 来年まで. It also follows a verb in the dictionary form: 雨がやむまで待つ (wait until the rain stops). Before a noun it takes の: 駅までの道.

The verb must be something that lasts: waiting, working, staying, walking. If the action happens once and you mean it must be done before the line (hand in, arrive, finish), you need までに, not まで. A separate use, まで meaning even (子供まで知っている), is not this skill.
patterns: [place] まで [歩く / 行く / 送る]

examples.jp: 五時[ごじ]{まで}働[はたら]きます。
駅[えき]{まで}歩[ある]きました。
授業[じゅぎょう]は九時[くじ]から三時[さんじ]{まで}です。
examples.en: Classes are from nine to three.

examples.jp: 東京[とうきょう]から大阪[おおさか]{まで}新幹線[しんかんせん]で行[い]きました。
examples.en: I went from Tokyo to Osaka by bullet train.

examples.jp: 最後[さいご]{まで}読[よ]みましたか。
examples.en: Did you read it to the end?

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]がやむ{まで}ここで待[ま]ちましょう。
examples.en: Let's wait here until the rain stops.

contrast.note: までに is a deadline for a one-off action: 五時までに帰る (be home by five). まで needs an action that keeps going up to the line: 五時まで待つ (wait until five).
から is the other end of the stretch, where it starts: 九時から is from nine, 九時まで until nine.
駅に行く names the destination; 駅まで行く stresses how far you go (as far as the station, and no further). With verbs that describe the movement itself (歩く, 走る, 泳ぐ) the end point takes まで; に sounds wrong.

mistakes.bad: 九時[くじ]{までに}働[はたら]きます。
mistakes.good: 九時[くじ]{まで}働[はたら]きます。
mistakes.note: Working goes on up to nine, so it is until (まで), not by (までに).

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]{に}歩[ある]きました。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]{まで}歩[ある]きました。
mistakes.note: 歩く describes the movement itself, so its end point takes まで. With 行く, に is fine: 駅に行きました.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]が来[く]る{までに}待[ま]ちます。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]が来[く]る{まで}待[ま]ちます。
mistakes.note: Waiting fills the whole time until the friend arrives, so it takes まで.

skills.tip: Does the action keep going right up to the line? Then まで. If it only has to happen once before the line, add に.

skills.rule: The deadline before which a one-off action must happen takes までに: by.
skills.explain:
までに sets a deadline. The action happens once, at any moment up to that point: 金曜日までに出す (hand it in by Friday), 五時までに帰る (be home by five). It is まで plus に: に pins a point, まで sets the limit, so together they mean at some point no later than.

The verb is a one-off event: hand in, arrive, finish, decide, reply, get married. Like まで, it attaches to relative time words (明日までに, 来週までに) and to a dictionary-form verb: 子供が起きるまでに (by the time the children get up).

The edge is with まで and plain に. まで is for an action that continues until the line; までに for one that must be done before it. Plain に gives the exact moment: 五時に出す is hand it in at five, 五時までに出す any time up to five. Also keep で apart: 今月で辞める means the end of this month is when I stop, not a deadline for a task.

examples.jp: 金曜日[きんようび]{までに}出[だ]してください。
examples.en: Please hand it in by Friday.

examples.jp: 五時[ごじ]{までに}帰[かえ]ります。
examples.en: I will be home by five.

examples.jp: 来週[らいしゅう]{までに}返事[へんじ]をします。
examples.en: I will reply by next week.

examples.jp: 明日[あした]{までに}この本[ほん]を読[よ]んでおいてください。
examples.en: Please finish reading this book by tomorrow.

examples.jp: 子供[こども]が起[お]きる{までに}朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]を作[つく]ります。
examples.en: I make breakfast before the children get up.

examples.jp: 三十歳[さんじゅっさい]{までに}結婚[けっこん]したいです。
examples.en: I want to get married by the time I am thirty.

contrast.note: まで is until, for something that keeps going: 金曜日まで休む (be off until Friday). までに is by, for something done once: 金曜日までに決める (decide by Friday).
に fixes the exact moment: 三時に来てください is come at three. 三時までに来てください is come by three, any time before is fine.
で after a time marks where a span ends: 今日で終わり (it ends today), 今月で辞める (I leave at the end of this month). It does not set a deadline for doing something.

mistakes.bad: 金曜日[きんようび]{まで}レポートを出[だ]してください。
mistakes.good: 金曜日[きんようび]{までに}レポートを出[だ]してください。
mistakes.note: Handing in happens once, so the deadline needs までに; まで would mean keep handing it in until Friday.

mistakes.bad: 雨[あめ]は夜[よる]{までに}降[ふ]り続[つづ]きました。
mistakes.good: 雨[あめ]は夜[よる]{まで}降[ふ]り続[つづ]きました。
mistakes.note: Raining on and on is an action that lasts, so it takes まで (until), not までに.

skills.tip: Translate it: if English says by, use までに; if it says until or till, use まで.
